page: Amazon Web Services t8i.nano is an entry-level burstable instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core across 2 threads using an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked up to 3.9 GHz. It features 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 0.5 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz (0.25 GB per core). The hardware configuration includes no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local instance storage, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results for the t8i.nano reflect its burstable multi-tenant profile and constrained core footprint. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core CPU performance scored 1957.34, categorizing it in the middle 50% average range across cloud instances. However, due to its low physical core count and thread-sharing design, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance reached 1993.79, placing it in the bottom 10% poor tier. Networking baseline bandwidth is designated at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

From an efficiency perspective, the t8i.nano operates as a low-overhead computing tier offering minimal baseline infrastructure cost for intermittent compute patterns. Tradeoffs are evident in the strict 0.5 GB memory limit and the burstable CPU allocation, which limits sustained heavy workloads. The platform includes modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-level encryption flags (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Appropriate workloads are restricted to lightweight background automation, low-traffic health checks, minimal microservices, and transient utility tasks.
